Distance decay of similarity

Source: R/beta.R
beta_decay.Rd

Pairs the pairwise beta diversity from beta_pair() with the distance between sites along a gradient, such as elevation, to study how dissimilarity and its components change with distance.

Usage

beta_decay(
  data,
  gradient,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  index = c("sorensen", "jaccard", "bray"),
  .by = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

gradient

<tidy-select> One or more numeric site attributes, constant within each site. With one column (such as elevation) the distance is the absolute difference; with several (such as c(x, y) coordinates) it is the Euclidean distance.

site, species

<tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

abundance

<tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

index

Family of dissimilarity: "sorensen" or "jaccard" (presence and absence) or "bray" (abundance-based Bray-Curtis).

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, kept in the output. Grouped data frames are also respected.

Value

A td_beta_decay tibble like the output of beta_pair(), with distance and, for a single gradient column, gradient_1 and gradient_2. Use ggplot2::autoplot() to plot it.

Examples

decay <- beta_decay(png_ants, gradient = elevation, .by = season)
decay
